newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-El Paso CEO sees $1 bln cash flow.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-El Paso CEO sees $1 bln cash flow.

text.p: El Paso Energy Corp will generate $1 billion of free cash flow from its operations during the next five years and will use it to invest in new growth projects, Chief Executive Officer William Wise said on Tuesday.

Wise said in an interview that the company, which acquired Tenneco Energy in 1996 for $4 billion, expects to generate annual cash flow of at least $200 million in the next five years, excluding maintenance capital, interest and dividends.

"All of that will be available for growth projects," Wise told Reuters after an annual meeting of shareholders in Dallas. "That is the engine for our growth. ...It's home-grown business opportunities -- more gathering and processing, more intrastate pipelines and more international projects."

He said about one-third of the new investment would go into domestic non-regulated markets, about one-third into international projects, notably in Latin America, Eastern Europe and Australasia, and about one-third into regulated U.S. markets.

"With that free cash flow and the investment opportunities, we can grow our earnings between 10 and 15 per cent per year in the forseeable future and we feel the high end of that range is not unreasonable," Wise said.

He said he expected annual earnings per share growth of about 15 percent in the next couple of years, and that he had no problem with analysts' expectations that El Paso would report first-quarter earnings per share of about $0.83.
"I am not uncomfortable with that," Wise said.
The company is to release its quarterly earnings report on April 24.

Wise said El Paso would focus more of its attention on non-regulated markets because they bring better growth rates and rates of return, but he stressed that the Houston-based company's future growth prospects were not tied to the growing trend of combining gas and electricity services.

"We are uniquely situated because of the geographic breadth of our assets to play a significant role in the convergence of gas and electricity, but it is not essential for our growth. We are very carefully watching it and participating where it makes sense," he said.
The acquisition of Tenneco Energy gave El Paso a coast-to-coast natural gas pipeline system.
Wise said the merger has been completed and that the number of employees in the combined companies has fallen to 3,400 from about 5,300 in early 1996.
